title: lcw-mercury-world-heavyweight
label: Harbinger
how: Def. Pariah by submission (Master Dreadlock) in an "I Quit" match, becoming the first Mercury World Heavyweight Champion.

title: lcw-mercury-world-heavyweight
label: Pariah
how: Def. Harbinger (c) by referee's decision, after both men were counted down together in a No-DQ shootfight refereed by David Beaumont.
note: Immediately after the decision, Gol and Magnum Wolf attacked Pariah and Beaumont and declared themselves the Oblivion on camera.

title: lcw-mercury-world-heavyweight
label: Geoffrey Slate
how: Def. Gol (c) on an uncaptured show, the title change evidenced only by the federation's own 27 May 2002 newsdesk item ("Because of Geoffrey Slate's victory over Gol, his match with Jin Akujin will be for the Mercury title!") and by Slate's own victory post on the roleplay board the same day ("Hey, I won. The first world title I've ever earned"). No results page for the match survives; the reign is the shortest in the belt's own short life per the roster's own reckoning (Jin Akujin's own roleplay of 30 May 2002: "He doesn't want to have the shortest title reign in the history of Mercury. Something that Gol currently has the record of" — spoken while Slate already held the belt, i.e. Gol's own reign, not Slate's, is the one being called shortest).
note: Still champion when the surviving record runs out: named defending champion in the promotion's own 30 May roleplay-board Mercury-title preview, the 10 June Climax-predictions thread ("Geoffrey Slate vs Harbinger vs Jin Akujin"), and thesupremebookingwarlord's own 14 June forum post ("You think I'd let somebody sucky hold the big belt?").

title: lcw-mercury-world-heavyweight
label: Gol
how: Def. Pariah (c) by pinfall (Fall From Grace) in a four-way elimination match also involving Magnum Wolf and Geoffrey Slate, becoming Oblivion's own first Mercury World Champion.

title: lcw-mercury-north-american
label: Memosarks
how: Def. Blaze McCoy in a Ladder Match to become the first North American Champion.

title: lcw-mercury-north-american
label: Magnum Wolf
how: Def. Memosarks (c) by pinfall (Magnum Force) in his own Mercury return match.

title: lcw-mercury-north-american
label: Geoffrey Slate
how: Became the third North American Champion by escaping a steel cage at the Silent Nightmare pay-per-view, per the federation's own brief-history recap ("Geoffrey Slate narrowly escapes the confines of a steel cage to become the third North American champion"). The show's own results page was never captured; the summary is the fed's own primary account, not a full transcript.

title: lcw-mercury-north-american
label: The Gol
how: Def. Geoffrey Slate (c) by pinfall (Alpha Driver from Magnum Wolf, off a Josh Trent distraction) to win the North American Championship.

title: lcw-mercury-north-american
label: Dirge
how: Def. Gol (c) by pinfall (fisherman's suplex with a bridge) to win the North American Championship, EEI security ringside.
note: Still champion when the surviving record runs out: defended against Robert Young at Suicide (5 May 2002) and billed against Hollow on the 10 June Climax-predictions thread's own card.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: The Trents
how: Beat The Graduates (Jerry Cane & Scott Tibor) to become the first Mercury Tag Team Champions, on the first Fusion after the belts were stripped from Evo's own Dean Wallace and Frank Heimdal in the LCW split.
note: The show's own results page was never captured; dated and sourced from the federation's own brief-history recap.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: Sloan and Matt Godsey
how: Def. The Trents (c) by pinfall (Foreclosure of a Dream) to win the Mercury Tag Team Championship, in their own second match as a team.
note: Sloan turned on Godsey moments later, dropping him with a Rag Doll slam and a top-rope bump; Godsey did not appear again holding the titles.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: Sloan and Slingshot
how: Sloan retained the belts with a new partner, Slingshot, defeating Legion (Myrddin & Barabbas) by pinfall the week after turning on Matt Godsey. No title change is recorded — the same champion, Sloan, simply named a new co-holder — so this row exists to track the holder change honestly rather than to claim a second title win.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: The Trents
how: Regained the Mercury Tag Team Championship from Sloan and Slingshot. The show's own results page was never captured; dated and sourced from the federation's own brief-history recap.
note: Retained against Entropy Crusade at Mercury Rising (13 November 2001) and fought Glamour & Picasso to a time-limit draw on 7 December 2001, keeping the belts both times.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: Picasso and Glamour
how: Def. The Trents (c) by pinfall (Starry Night shooting star press) to win the Mercury Tag Team Championship as EEI; defended once more as "The Elite" against Headbuster & Inferno on 22 February 2002.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: Dirge and Picasso
how: David Beaumont reassigned Johnny Glamour's own half of the tag titles to Dirge without a match, forming Ultimate Refinement — in Dirge's own words, "Dave Beaumont GAVE me the belt with complete confidence rather than putting it up for grabs" (roleplay of 9 April 2002). Already the recognized champions by the 29 March 2002 Fusion and by the federation's own champions.html (captured 16 April 2002: "Tag Team Champions: EEI (currently Picasso & Dirge)"); the exact date of the reassignment is not stated and is bounded only between the 6 February 2002 title change and 29 March 2002 — recorded here as a presumed midpoint, not a fact.
note: Retained against The Trents and The Heat Seekers in a triple threat on 29 March 2002 and against the same two teams again on 5 April 2002.

title: lcw-mercury-tag-team
label: The Elite
how: Dirge relinquished his own half of the tag titles to Picasso on air on 12 April 2002 ("I give up my half of the tag team titles, and the chapter of our lives known as EEI...is closed"), dissolving EEI; Johnny Glamour returned the following week and resumed as Picasso's own tag partner, reforming as the Elite. The federation's own brief-history recap dates the return to 19 April 2002; that show's own results page was never captured.
note: Still champions when the surviving record runs out: retained against The Trents in a Salt Lake City Streetfight at Suicide (5 May 2002) and billed against Rush & Killjoy on the 10 June Climax-predictions thread's own card.
